observed_behavior: The legal build-input policy in strict JSON had no supported source-owned implementation annotation.
expected_behavior: Identify the implementing input objects without sidecar maps, schema violations or attributing policy to the generic engine.
causal_mechanism: Discovery admitted only source comments while strict build-impact V2 input schemas allowed only kind and path.

anti_pattern.structural_description: The annotation contract assumed every implementing source format supports comments.
anti_pattern.why_it_fails: Strict JSON policy objects cannot carry those comments and reject undeclared metadata fields.

correct_pattern.required_invariant: Annotations belong to actual implementing source objects and must conform to the owning physical schema.
correct_pattern.implementation_description: V3 inputs allow canonical traceability arrays; strict JSON discovery reads only those object-local properties, rejects duplicate keys, and reuses the existing relationship parser. V1/V2 remain exact.

applicability_conditions: An implementation is owned by a strict JSON object whose schema supports the annotation field
known_non_matches: Ordinary JSON strings and JSON test declarations do not provide coverage.
confirmation_evidence: The client V2 input parser rejected the new field; V3 real input queries and object-local graph discovery pass with an isolated portable runtime.
regression_proofs: tests/build-impact.test.js: V3 source-owned annotations preserve real legal input selection and V1/V2 exact schemas
tests/traceability-discovery.test.ts: JSON annotations belong to their actual object and preserve source lines
tests/traceability-discovery.test.ts: JSON discovery rejects duplicate properties, malformed annotations and fake test declarations
